result.title: Beyond Appearance: Where Forest Visual Place Recognition Actually Fails
result.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, accepted to the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA)
result.summary: Visual place recognition (VPR) in forest environments remains challenging because repetitive vegetation, and changes in illumination, season, and viewpoint can make distinct places appear similar and revisited places appear substantially different. In this paper, we investigate whether temporal, linguistic, structural, and geometric context can improve on an appearance-only descriptor, and what limits each representation when it does not. Using MegaLoc as the appearance-based baseline on the WildCross benchmark, we evaluate score-space and descriptor-space sequence matching, vision-language captions and reranking, scene-graph representations, and depth-derived stem graphs across same-direction revisits, extended routes, and reverse traversals. On a same-direction revisit, both sequence matching strategies reach similar Recall@1 (94.1% vs. 91.5%), but recall at 100% precision rises from 50.9% (single-frame MegaLoc) to 71.6% in score space and falls to 36.5% in descriptor space. The remaining context representations provide no consistent improvement over the appearance-based baseline. Same-place captions show limited place-specific discrimination, reranking is constrained by the initial candidate shortlist, and stem-graph matching remains weak even with LiDAR depth.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在森林视觉地点识别任务上，以 MegaLoc 为仅外观基线，在 WildCross 基准上系统比较序列匹配、视觉语言描述与重排、场景图及深度主干图等多种时序/语言/结构/几何上下文表示，并分析各自失效的原因。
AI.relevance_reason: 其负结果提示「增加上下文表示并不必然提升判别力」，且重排受初始候选列表限制，可能可供核查 latent 推理中视觉证据筛选与候选取证瓶颈的类比问题，但任务与机制均相距较远。
